newsitem.title: USA: Lone Star Steakhouse stock hurt after earnings outlook.
newsitem.headline: Lone Star Steakhouse stock hurt after earnings outlook.

text.p: The stock of Lone Star Steakhouse & Saloon Inc. tumbled over 17 percent in heavy trading Tuesday after the company said its third-quarter profits would not meet analysts' expectations.
After the market's close Monday, Lone Star said it expects its third-quarter earnings to be 10 cents to 13 cents a share below analysts' forecasts.

According to First Call, 10 analysts were estimating Lone Star's third-quarter earnings in a range of 45 cents to 50 cents a share, with a mean estimate of 47 cents. The company earned 38 cents a share in the 1996 quarter
Lone Star's stock was down $4.1875 to $17.8125 in midday trading on Nasdaq.
Comparable store sales were down 11.1 percent quarter-to-date, bringing year-to-date comparable store sales to negative 7.7 percent, Lone Star said.

Lone Star cited reduced margins due to a "continued decline in average unit volumes" in the first part of the current quarter and planned spending on advertising and marketing in the last half of the year.

"The casual dining environment is likely to remain extremely competitive for some time, without any near-term relief in sight," Jefferies analysts David Rose and James Pott said in a report. "As a consequence, Lone Star will likely see same store sales pressure continuing into the first quarter."

Lone Star, based in Wichita, Kan., owns and operates 230 domestic and 24 international Lone Star Steakhouse & Saloon restaurants; two Sullivan's Steakhouse restaurants; and three Del Frisco's Double Eagle Steak House restaurants.
